| [THEORY-134](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md) v2 | Whether a system can persist is a question about a constraint set fixed independently of its dynamics: a set is viable when from each of its states some evolution can stay in it, and when it is not, its viability kernel is the largest part that is, from the rest of which every evolution leaves in finite time | Aubin's viability theory, read in his 1999 mini-course notes [LIT-714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-714.md). Given dynamics and a set K of required states, K is viable if some evolution from each state stays in K and invariant if every one does. Nagumo's theorem reduces viability to a tangency condition. The viability kernel is the largest viable subset of K; from outside it every evolution exits K. The notes do not compare viability with stability; that contrast is a further step. | Active |
| [THEORY-771](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-771.md) v4 | In a singularly perturbed system, fast states x̃ with dx̃/dt = f̃(x̃, y) + ε·δf and slow states y with dy/dt = ε·ḡ(y) + ε·δg, if f̃ is contracting in x̃ at rate β_f with x̃ = 0 an equilibrium for every y, ḡ is contracting at rate β_g, and \|δf\| ≤ d_f + α_f,x\|x̃\| + α_f,y\|y\|, \|δg\| ≤ d_g + α_g,x\|x̃\|, then for every ε below ε_c = β_f / [χ_f(α_f,x + χ_g α_f,y α_g,x / β_g)] the fast states stay within O(ε) of zero and, when d_g = 0, the slow states within O(ε) of the reduced trajectory, uniformly in time after a transient of order (1/β_f + 1/(εβ_g)) log(1/ε) | Bousquet and Slotine (arXiv 2015), [LIT-1292](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1292.md), read in [NOTE-1025](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1025.md). It gives Simon's near-decomposability the rate in ε that [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md)'s open statement lacks: first order, for trajectory error, uniform in time, under contraction of the modules and of the reduced slow system, with an explicit, sufficient ceiling on ε. Deterministic. It bounds how far the states are from the reduced description, not how much information the rest of the system sends into the slow variables, and it takes the slow coordinates as given. | Active |
| [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) v2 | In a singularly perturbed system ẋ = f(x, z, t), εż = g(x, z, ε), if g is contracting in z at rate λ_z for every x and ε, the reduced system ẋ = f(x, γ(x), t) on the slow manifold z = γ(x) is contracting at rate λ_x, f is α-Lipschitz in z, \|∂γ/∂x · f\| ≤ d and g is K-Lipschitz in ε, then for all t ≥ 0 the fast state is within χ_z e^{−λ_z t/ε}\|z(0) − γ(x(0))\| + εχ_z(d + K)/λ_z of the manifold and the slow state within χ_x\|x(0) − x_γ(0)\|e^{−λ_x t} + ε[C₁(e^{−λ_x t} − e^{−λ_z t/ε}) + C₂(1 − e^{−λ_x t})] of the reduced trajectory; partial contraction of f in x alone is not enough | Del Vecchio and Slotine (IEEE TAC 2013), [LIT-1295](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1295.md), read in [NOTE-1020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1020.md), with their Theorem 3's hypothesis corrected. A global, uniform-in-time, first-order bound on the error of the quasi-steady-state reduction, with every constant explicit and no requirement that ε be small. The reduction is Markovian: eliminating a fast, contracting variable costs O(ε) in trajectory error for all time, so no memory term is needed to that order. Constant metrics, deterministic, and the bound d on how fast the manifold moves is needed along the trajectory. | Active |
| [THEORY-1254](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1254.md) | A controller that must stay safe under every model it has not ruled out cannot use the evidence its committing action produces: if the information it can gather before its first action that forecloses a safe continuation under an alternative is bounded by β, every such controller forfeits at least about ½e^{−β} of the value reachable only by committing, so a linear oracle gap gives linear regret, and acting on an exclusion at risk α needs about log(1/(2α)) nats gathered beforehand | Saligrama (2026), [LIT-1880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1880.md), Theorem 1 and its examples, read in [NOTE-1466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1466.md). The proof is data processing on the stopped record plus Bretagnolle–Huber, and the explicit relaxation and one example's optimization were checked numerically. Active: a theorem with a short proof, checked. It is a lower bound only; bounded information is sufficient for an unavoidable gap, and unbounded information does not by itself give recovery. | Active |
